questions.question: Who among the following is the final interpreter of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The Supreme Court of India is the apex judicial body and the final interpreter of the Constitution. It has the power of Judicial Review to ensure that laws passed by Parliament or actions taken by the Executive do not violate the constitutional framework.

questions.question: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, what is the punishment for mob lynching?
questions.solution: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, introduced Section 103(2) specifically for mob lynching. It mandates that if a group of five or more people commits murder based on race, caste, sex, or belief, they shall be punished with death or life imprisonment and a fine.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct in the context of constitutional interpretation and judicial doctrine?
questions.option_1: The Constitution of India clearly defines the term "basic structure" under Article 368.
questions.option_2: The Judiciary rejected the idea of spirit-based interpretation and strictly follows the written text.
questions.option_3: The "basic structure" doctrine was brought into existence by the Supreme Court to protect the fundamental features of the Constitution.
questions.option_4: The Parliament can propose amendments that repeal judicial principles without limitation.
questions.solution: The Basic Structure Doctrine was established in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973). It dictates that while Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution under Article 368, it cannot alter the fundamental features that form its core identity.

questions.question: According to Section 21 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, which of the following statements is correct regarding the trial of offences under Sections 64 to 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
questions.option_1: The trial must be conducted by any police officer of the rank of DSP and above.
questions.option_2: These offences must be tried only in a High Court under a male judge.
questions.option_3: Such offences are exclusively triable by Executive Magistrates.
questions.option_4: These offences shall, as far as practicable, be tried by a court presided over by a woman.
questions.solution: Section 21 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) focuses on gender sensitivity. It stipulates that trials for sexual offences (Sections 64-71 of BNS) should, as far as practicable, be presided over by a woman judge to provide a more comfortable environment for victims.

questions.question: Which of the following High Courts has jurisdiction over more than one state?
questions.solution:
The Guwahati High Court currently holds jurisdiction over four states: Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, and Arunachal Pradesh.
Note:
  • Kerala HC: Kerala and Lakshadweep (1 state, 1 UT).
  • Delhi HC: Only Delhi (UT).
  • Patna HC: Only Bihar (1 state).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.option_1: Article 30 of the Constitution of India gives the Supreme Court wide original jurisdiction.
questions.option_2: Original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more states.
questions.option_3: The Supreme Court has very wide advisory jurisdiction over all courts and tribunals in India.
questions.option_4: The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court can be exercised by a certificate granted by the High Court.
questions.solution:
Under Article 131, the Supreme Court has Original Jurisdiction. This means it is the first and only court to hear disputes between:
  • The Centre and one or more States.
  • The Centre and any State(s) on one side and other State(s) on the other.
  • Two or more States.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the first-ever motion to remove a Supreme Court Justice in India:
A. The first motion to remove a Supreme Court Judge was signed in 1991 by 108 Members of Parliament.
B. It was filed against Justice V. Ramaswami for alleged misconduct during his tenure as Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court.
Which one of the above statements is correct?
questions.solution: Statement A is correct. Statement B is incorrect because the allegations against Justice V. Ramaswami pertained to his tenure as Chief Justice of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, not the Allahabad High Court.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India grants power to the President to appoint Judges of the Supreme Court?
questions.solution: Article 124(2) states that every Judge of the Supreme Court shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal after consultation with such of the Judges of the Supreme Court and of the High Courts in the States as the President may deem necessary.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India comprises the Chief Justice and not more than ______ other Judges appointed by the President of India.
questions.solution: Currently, the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court is 34 judges (1 Chief Justice + 33 other judges). This was increased from 31 (30+1) via the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Constitution:
A. Articles 214 to 231 in Part VI deal with the High Courts in the states.
B. These Articles provide for the organization, independence, jurisdiction, powers, and procedures of the High Courts.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both A and B are correct. Part VI of the Constitution contains the provisions for the state executive, legislature, and the High Courts (Articles 214-231).

questions.question: Which writ is issued by a high court or supreme court when a lower court has considered a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
questions.solution: The writ of Prohibition is issued by a higher court to a lower court or quasi-judicial body to stop it from proceeding in a case where it does not have legal jurisdiction.

questions.question: In which judgement did the Supreme Court extend the scope of Article 21 and observed that ‘the Right to education flows directly from the ‘Right to life’?
questions.option_1: Mohini Jain v State of Karnataka
questions.option_2: Neerja Choudhari v State of M. P.
questions.option_3: Kharak Singh v State of UP
questions.option_4: Malak Singh v State of Punjab
questions.solution: In the Mohini Jain case (1992), the Supreme Court held that the right to education is a fundamental right that stems from the Right to Life (Article 21), as dignity and life are incomplete without education.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all the courts within the territory of India?
questions.solution: Article 141 establishes the principle of stare decisis at the national level, making the Supreme Court's legal rulings binding on all subordinate courts in India.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India?
A. Original jurisdiction extends to any dispute between the Government of India and one or more States or between the Government of India and any State or States on one side and one or more States on the other or between two or more States.
B. Appellate Jurisdiction extends when the Union plus some States are one side and some other States on the other side of the dispute.
C. Under Articles 129 and 142 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court has been vested with the power to punish for contempt of court.
D. As of now, the International Commercial Arbitration cannot be initiated in the Supreme Court.
questions.solution: Statement A is correct (Original jurisdiction under Article 131). Statement C is correct (Article 129 makes SC a court of record with power to punish for contempt). Statement B is incorrect because that scenario still falls under Original jurisdiction, not Appellate. Statement D is incorrect as the SC does handle international commercial arbitrations.

questions.question: The advisory board under provisions of Article 22 of the Constitution is to consist of persons who are, or have been or are qualified to be appointed as __________.
questions.solution: Article 22 deals with protection against arrest and detention. It states that no person can be detained under preventive detention for more than three months unless an Advisory Board, consisting of persons qualified to be High Court Judges, reports sufficient cause for extended detention.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Federal Court of India:
A. The Federal Court of India was established in Delhi under the Government of India Act, 1935, and started functioning from 1937.
B. It served as the highest judicial body in India until it was replaced by the Supreme Court of India in 1950.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both A and B are correct. The Federal Court was the predecessor to the Supreme Court. It functioned from 1937 until the inauguration of the Supreme Court on January 28, 1950.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Supreme Court of India:
A. Article 124 of the Indian Constitution provides that there shall be a Supreme Court of India.
B. Article 121 deals with restrictions on discussion in Parliament regarding the conduct of judges of the Supreme Court or a High Court.
questions.solution: Both A and B are correct. Article 124 establishes the court, while Article 121 protects judicial independence by forbidding Parliamentary discussion on a judge's conduct (except during impeachment).

questions.question: Disputes between two or more states come under the _______ of the Supreme Court.
questions.solution: Disputes between states are handled directly and exclusively by the Supreme Court under its Original Jurisdiction (Article 131).

questions.question: In which of the following cases the Supreme Court, while laying out the 'basic structure' of the Constitution held that the democratic character of the polity was an essential component of the 'basic structure"?
questions.option_1: Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras
questions.option_2: AK Gopalan vs State of Madras
questions.option_3: Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala
questions.option_4: Sajjan Singh vs State of Rajasthan
questions.solution: The Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) is the landmark judgment that introduced the Basic Structure doctrine and identified democracy as one of its essential components.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding important Supreme Court judgments:
A. In the State of Kerala vs Leesamma Joseph case, the Supreme Court held that persons with disabilities are entitled to reservation in promotions under Article 16.
B. In the Shayara Bano vs Union of India case, the Supreme Court struck down the practice of triple talaq as unconstitutional.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both A and B are correct. The Leesamma Joseph case focused on rights for disabled persons, and the Shayara Bano case (2017) banned instant Triple Talaq.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India came into existence on ___________.
questions.solution: The Supreme Court of India was established on January 26, 1950, the day India became a Republic. It was formally inaugurated two days later on January 28, 1950.

questions.question: Till which year did the High Court of Delhi continue to exercise jurisdiction over Himachal Pradesh?
questions.solution: The Delhi High Court exercised jurisdiction over Himachal Pradesh until 1971, when Himachal Pradesh was granted full statehood and its own High Court was established.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the Family Courts (Amendment) Bill, 2022?
1. The Family Courts (Amendment) Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on 18 July 2022.
2. The Bill amends the Family Courts Act, 1984.
3. The Act allows state governments to establish Family Courts.
4. The Act is not applicable in Punjab and Tamil Nadu.
questions.solution: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct. The Amendment specifically aimed to validate family courts in Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland. Statement 4 is incorrect as the Act is broadly applicable across India.

questions.question: The High court of Delhi was established in ______.
questions.solution: The Delhi High Court was established on October 31, 1966. Before this, Delhi fell under the jurisdiction of the Punjab High Court.

questions.question: The first High Court in India was established in ______________.
questions.solution: The first High Court in India was the Calcutta High Court, established on July 1, 1862, under the High Courts Act of 1861.
